findings.title: 1 vulnerable dependency with 3 known vulnerabilities
findings.detail:
Detected via OSV.dev against exact locked versions:
• brace-expansion@5.0.6 (npm) — 3 known vulns: GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp, GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895
Full list with links in the Dependencies section.

findings.title: Almost no docstrings/JSDoc (0% of 183 functions)
findings.detail: Document public functions at minimum — the exported API surface.

findings.title: No coverage reporting configured
findings.detail: Add coverage (istanbul/vitest/pytest-cov) + a codecov/upload step to track the trend.

findings.title: 1 very large directory (≥50 source files)
findings.detail:
• tests/ (110 files)
Group by feature/domain instead of dumping everything together.

plan.title: Patch vulnerable dependencies
plan.detail: Run the ecosystem audit (npm audit / pip-audit / cargo audit), bump affected packages, and wire the audit into CI so regressions fail the build.

plan.title: Refactor the highest-complexity functions
plan.detail: Start with the top 5 offenders: extract helpers, replace branch chains with early returns and lookup tables. Target cx ≤ 10 per function.

plan.title: Split god files into focused modules
plan.detail: Group by responsibility (parsing, IO, orchestration) and extract classes/modules; keep files under ~300 lines.

plan.title: Extract shared helpers from duplicated blocks
plan.detail: The flagged clones drift apart silently — consolidate each group into one function.

plan.title: Add coverage reporting
plan.detail: Enable coverage in the test runner and upload to codecov so the trend is visible.

plan.title: Adopt a docstring/JSDoc convention
plan.detail: Document all exported functions first; enforce with eslint-plugin-jsdoc / ruff pydocstyle.

plan.title: Reorganize oversized directories
plan.detail: Group files by feature/domain to restore navigability.

notes: Partial analysis: 216 of 217 files were analyzed (size/file-count caps). Scores are still representative but not exhaustive.
